name: Electric Bicycle
description: A bicycle or tricycle with fully operable pedals, a seat or saddle, and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph. Defined by Wyoming Statutes §31-1-101(a)(xxxiv) and regulated by §31-5-707, both from SF 81 (2019), effective July 1, 2019.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; Class 2 can propel the bike without pedaling but can't assist past 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling and stops at 28 mph
Two or three wheels, fully operable pedals, a seat or saddle, and a motor of less than 750 watts
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512), and the motor assist stops when the rider stops pedaling, brakes or disengages the motor
Manufacturers and distributors must permanently affix a label in at least 9-point type stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its motor-powered speed or engagement unless the label is replaced to match
No statewide minimum age or helmet requirement
The rider has the rights and duties of the driver of any vehicle, as a bicyclist does
Motorists passing one must leave at least three feet where space allows
A local authority or state agency may regulate any class on trails it manages, including natural-surface nonmotorized trails
Local authorities may regulate e-bike operation on their streets and may require e-bikes to be registered and licensed, for a fee
Not a motor vehicle, moped, motorcycle or motor-driven cycle: no driver's license, state registration, title, insurance or off-road recreational vehicle rules
